title: goal-pulse-hacklog-amber-kim
content:
HACKLOG: Q1 personal goal pulse (working scratchpad)

Context: quick, messy log for tracking the personal OKRs I own/contribute to. Not a finalized doc — mostly a place to capture progress, micro-experiments, blockers, and random ideas that might become playbooks.

High-level objectives I care about (personal lens):
- Obj A: Improve end-to-end latency experience shipped by the hosted API team (focus on 95th pct).
  - KR A1: Move 95th p95 from ~420ms -> <= 340ms for small text-gen requests (<=512 tokens) by end of Q1.
  - KR A2: Validate one cache strategy in prod that reduces repeat request cost by 10%.
- Obj B: Reduce per-token infra cost on our dedicated pools for common inference shapes.
  - KR B1: Identify two models + quantization config pairs with >=15% unit-cost reduction and <2% quality regression (measured by evaluation set).
- Obj C: Personal craft: ship 2 developer-facing docs/tooling updates that make A/B rollouts easier for small teams.

Today (3/10) quick notes:
- Small wins: latency spike from last week traced to missing KV-cache eviction heuristics in one serving path. Patch landed (PR #541), rolling canary. Observed ~30ms median improvement in canary region after patch. Need more data on p95.
- Experiment: enabling prefix caching for repeated greeting prompts on canary subset. Early signal: cache hit rate 12% across sampled workload; cost down ~4% for those flows. Still noisy.
- Blocking: need infra quota bump for canary fleet to scale to 20% traffic — awaiting infra-requests approval from Samir. (Follow-up: ping infra on Monday)

Open hypotheses (brain-dump):
- H1: A small-target cache (per-customer recent prefixes) will disproportionately reduce p95 for interactive chat because it avoids re-evaluating shared prefix tokens.
  - Quick test: run synthetic replay tests with 30% prefix reuse and measure p95 delta. (TODO: replay job ID LINEAR-RED-432)
- H2: Lightweight int8 quantization with a tuned kernel selection on T4/RTX will cut cost 12–18% with <1.5% eval-bleu drop on medium-length prompts. Need to pick 3 eval tasks.

Weekly micro-checklist (what I did / will do):
- Done: triaged latency alert, wrote quick playbook snippet for paging SRE when p95 > 500ms for 10m.
- Done: prototyped small replay harness to test prefix cache hypothesis (local only).
- Next: coordinate canary scale with infra (Samir) and get second region rolling.
- Next: schedule 30m sync w/ Jules to align on quantify/regression gating for quantization experiments.

Metrics snapshot (rough, from memory; reconcile with dashboards):
- Hosted API small-req p95: ~420ms (global); median ~120ms.
- Repeat-request hit-rate (approx): 8–12% depending on workload.
- Cost/unit (dedicated common shape): baseline 1.0 -> target 0.82 by end of Q1.

Personal retro notes (what felt off last sprint):
- I spent too much time digging into noisy traces; need to prioritize experiments that give clear, measurable deltas.
- Communication: I didn't loop in product early enough on tradeoffs for quantization vs. latency — caused rework. Fix: early 10-min alignment before big experiments.

Action items (short-lived, personal):
- AI-1: Add a short eval set (10 prompts each: short-chat, code, summarization) for quick quantization smoke tests. Target: finish by 3/17.
- AI-2: Create a minimal dashboard widget (p95 and cache-hit) for my team to monitor canary region. Ask Jules for a template.
- AI-3: Draft a 1-pager on canary scale plan + rollback criteria for infra approval. Drop in Samir's inbox by EOD Thursday.

Random ideas / playbook seeds (scribbles):
- If cache-hit <5% but p95 improves >5% -> likely noisy workload; rule out by segmenting by prompt length.
- Consider a lightweight per-route sampling of KV-cache contents for debugging (obfuscate content for PII).

Notes to self:
- When writing the 1-pager, include clear failure modes: wrong-model fallback, degraded-quality rollback, and billing surprise.
- Keep experiments small and reversible. Prefer canary by user cohort vs. all-traffic canary.

Quick meeting log (3/9 retro):
- Jules: wants clearer thresholds for quality regressions (suggest: eval delta >2% BLEU/QA accuracy).
- Samir: can give quota bump if we provide a one-paragraph justification + rollback checklist.

End-of-note micro-reflection: this doc is messy on purpose. The goal is to capture the friction points and hypotheses before they dissipate. Later: formalize into a short PRD or Confluence note if an experiment proves promising.

-- Amber

(Links to tickets: LINEAR-RED-412, LINEAR-RED-432; Slack: #eng-dx thread 123)
